stem:
Parallel lines $p$ and $q$ are cut by transversal $r$. One same-side interior angle measures $80^{\circ}$.

Which two claims correctly give the other same-side interior angle?

options.text: The other same-side interior angle is $100^{\circ}$, because same-side interior angles on parallel lines add to $180^{\circ}$.
The other same-side interior angle is $80^{\circ}$, because same-side interior angles on parallel lines are equal.
The other same-side interior angle is $180^{\circ}-80^{\circ}=100^{\circ}$.
The other same-side interior angle is $160^{\circ}$, from doubling $80^{\circ}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Same-side interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary: 180−80=100. Treating them as equal or doubling 80 misses that sum.
